# API Testing Guide

This guide provides examples for testing all API endpoints using curl commands or any HTTP client.

## Authentication Flow

### 1. Register a New User

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "password": "password123",
    "role": "CUSTOMER"
  }'
```

**Expected Response:**
```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid-here",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "role": "CUSTOMER"
  }
}
```

### 2. Login

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "password": "password123"
  }'
```

### 3. Refresh Token

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/refresh \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "refresh_token": "your_refresh_token_here"
  }'
```

## User Management Tests

### Get User Profile

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Get All Users (Admin Only)

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Update User

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/users/USER_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Updated Name"
  }'
```

## Vendor Management Tests

### Register as Vendor

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Vendor Store",
    "email": "vendor@example.com",
    "password": "password123",
    "role": "VENDOR"
  }'
```

### Get All Vendors

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/vendors
```

### Get Vendor Profile (Vendor Only)

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/vendors/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Update Vendor Profile

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/vendors/VENDOR_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Updated Vendor Name",
    "description": "We sell amazing products",
    "businessAddress": "123 Business Street",
    "phoneNumber": "+1234567890"
  }'
```

### Get Vendor Orders

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/vendors/me/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

## Product Management Tests

### Create Product (Vendor Only)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Gaming Laptop",
    "description": "High-performance gaming laptop with RTX graphics",
    "price": 1299.99,
    "stock": 10
  }'
```

### Get All Products with Pagination

```bash
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/products?page=1&limit=5&search=laptop"
```

### Get Products with Filters

```bash
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/products?minPrice=100&maxPrice=2000&vendorId=VENDOR_ID"
```

### Get Single Product

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/products/PRODUCT_ID
```

### Update Product

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/products/PRODUCT_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Updated Gaming Laptop",
    "price": 1399.99,
    "stock": 15
  }'
```

### Delete Product

```bash
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/products/PRODUCT_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Get Products by Vendor

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/products/vendor/VENDOR_ID
```

## Order Management Tests

### Create Order (Customer Only)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer CUSTOMER_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "productId": "PRODUCT_ID_1",
        "quantity": 2
      },
      {
        "productId": "PRODUCT_ID_2",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

### Get User Orders

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer CUSTOMER_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Get Single Order

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/orders/ORDER_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer CUSTOMER_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Update Order Status (Admin Only)

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/orders/ORDER_ID/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "status": "COMPLETED"
  }'
```

## Chat System Tests

### Send Message

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/chat/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "receiverId": "USER_ID",
    "message": "Hello, I need help with my order"
  }'
```

### Get Chat History

```bash
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/chat/history/USER_ID?page=1&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Get Conversations

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/chat/conversations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

### Get All Chats (Admin Only)

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/chat/admin/all \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

## WebSocket Testing

### JavaScript WebSocket Client Example

```javascript
// Install socket.io-client: npm install socket.io-client
const io = require('socket.io-client');

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', {
  auth: {
    token: 'YOUR_JWT_TOKEN'
  }
});

// Connection events
socket.on('connect', () => {
  console.log('Connected to server');
});

socket.on('connected', (data) => {
  console.log('Connection confirmed:', data);
});

// Send a message
socket.emit('sendMessage', {
  receiverId: 'USER_ID',
  message: 'Hello from WebSocket!'
});

// Listen for message confirmation
socket.on('messageSent', (message) => {
  console.log('Message sent successfully:', message);
});

// Listen for new messages
socket.on('newMessage', (message) => {
  console.log('New message received:', message);
});

// Send typing indicator
socket.emit('typing', {
  receiverId: 'USER_ID',
  isTyping: true
});

// Listen for typing indicators
socket.on('userTyping', (data) => {
  console.log(`User ${data.userId} is typing: ${data.isTyping}`);
});

// Error handling
socket.on('error', (error) => {
  console.error('Socket error:', error);
});
```

## Complete Test Workflow

Here's a complete workflow to test the entire system:

### 1. Setup Users

```bash
# Register Admin
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Admin User", "email": "admin@example.com", "password": "admin123", "role": "ADMIN"}'

# Register Vendor
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Tech Store", "email": "vendor@example.com", "password": "vendor123", "role": "VENDOR"}'

# Register Customer
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "John Customer", "email": "customer@example.com", "password": "customer123", "role": "CUSTOMER"}'
```

### 2. Create Products

```bash
# Login as vendor and create products
VENDOR_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "vendor@example.com", "password": "vendor123"}' | \
  jq -r '.access_token')

# Create first product
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VENDOR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Laptop", "description": "Gaming laptop", "price": 1299.99, "stock": 5}'

# Create second product
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VENDOR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Mouse", "description": "Gaming mouse", "price": 59.99, "stock": 20}'
```

### 3. Place Order

```bash
# Login as customer and place order
CUSTOMER_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "customer@example.com", "password": "customer123"}' | \
  jq -r '.access_token')

# Get products to find IDs
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/products

# Place order (replace PRODUCT_IDs with actual IDs)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items": [{"productId": "PRODUCT_ID_1", "quantity": 1}, {"productId": "PRODUCT_ID_2", "quantity": 2}]}'
```

### 4. Test Chat

```bash
# Send message from customer to vendor
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/chat/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"receiverId": "VENDOR_USER_ID", "message": "Hello, I have a question about my order"}'
```

## Error Handling Tests

### Test Invalid Authentication

```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer invalid_token"
```

### Test Insufficient Permissions

```bash
# Try to delete user as customer (should fail)
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/users/USER_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

### Test Invalid Data

```bash
# Try to create product with invalid data
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer VENDOR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "", "price": -10}'
```

## Performance Tests

### Test Pagination

```bash
# Test large page sizes
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/products?page=1&limit=100"
```

### Test Search Performance

```bash
# Test search with various terms
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/products?search=gaming"
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/products?search=laptop"
```

## Tips for Testing

1. **Save Tokens**: Save access tokens in environment variables for easier testing
2. **Use jq**: Install `jq` for JSON parsing in bash scripts
3. **Postman**: Import these curl commands into Postman for easier testing
4. **Test Scripts**: Create bash scripts for common test workflows
5. **Database State**: Reset database between major test runs for consistent results

version: '3.8'

services:
  # Database
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    container_name: multi-vendor-db
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DATABASE_NAME:-multi_vendor_db}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DATABASE_USER:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_PASSWORD:-password}
    ports:
      - "${DATABASE_PORT:-5432}:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./init-db.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init-db.sql
    networks:
      - multi-vendor-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${DATABASE_USER:-postgres}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # Redis for caching and sessions
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: multi-vendor-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${REDIS_PORT:-6379}:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    networks:
      - multi-vendor-network
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # Application
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      target: production
    container_name: multi-vendor-app
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${NODE_ENV:-production}
      PORT: ${PORT:-3000}
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${DATABASE_USER:-postgres}:${DATABASE_PASSWORD:-password}@postgres:5432/${DATABASE_NAME:-multi_vendor_db}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-your-super-secret-jwt-key-change-this-in-production}
      JWT_EXPIRES_IN: ${JWT_EXPIRES_IN:-15m}
      JWT_REFRESH_SECRET: ${JWT_REFRESH_SECRET:-your-super-secret-refresh-key-change-this-in-production}
      JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN: ${JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN:-7d}
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-3000}:3000"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - multi-vendor-network
    volumes:
      - ./uploads:/app/uploads
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 40s

  # Nginx reverse proxy
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    container_name: multi-vendor-nginx
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
      - ./ssl:/etc/nginx/ssl
    depends_on:
      - app
    networks:
      - multi-vendor-network

volumes:
  postgres_data:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local

networks:
  multi-vendor-network:
    driver: bridge

# Multi-Vendor Backend System with Real-Time Support

A comprehensive e-commerce backend system built with NestJS, featuring multi-vendor support, real-time notifications, and chat functionality.

## 🚀 Features

### Core Features
- **Multi-vendor marketplace** - Support for multiple vendors selling products
- **User authentication** - JWT-based authentication with role-based access control (Customer, Vendor, Admin)
- **Product management** - CRUD operations with advanced filtering and pagination
- **Order management** - Complete order lifecycle with status tracking
- **Real-time notifications** - WebSocket-based notifications for order status changes
- **Chat system** - Real-time messaging between customers, vendors, and admins

### Advanced Features
- **Role-based chat routing** - Automatic assignment of chat receivers based on user roles
- **Pagination** - Efficient pagination for product listings
- **WebSocket notifications** - Real-time order status updates via Socket.IO
- **Comprehensive API documentation** - Auto-generated Swagger documentation
- **Unit testing** - Test coverage for key services and controllers
- **Dockerization** - Complete Docker setup for development and production

### Technical Stack
- **Framework**: NestJS (Node.js)
- **Database**: PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM
- **Authentication**: JWT with bcryptjs
- **Real-time**: Socket.IO for WebSocket connections
- **Documentation**: Swagger/OpenAPI
- **Testing**: Jest
- **Containerization**: Docker & Docker Compose

## 📁 Project Structure

```
src/
├── auth/                 # Authentication module
│   ├── dto/             # Data transfer objects
│   ├── guards/          # Authentication guards
│   └── auth.service.ts  # Authentication logic
├── chat/                # Chat system module
│   ├── dto/             # Chat DTOs
│   └── chat.service.ts  # Chat business logic
├── health/              # Health check endpoint
├── notifications/       # WebSocket notifications
│   └── notifications.gateway.ts
├── orders/              # Order management
├── products/            # Product management
├── prisma/              # Database configuration
├── users/               # User management
└── vendors/             # Vendor management
```

## 🔧 Installation & Setup

### Prerequisites
- Node.js (18.x or later)
- PostgreSQL
- npm or yarn

### Local Development Setup

1. **Clone the repository**
   ```bash
   git clone <repository-url>
   cd Multi-Vendor-Backend-System-with-Real-Time-Support
   ```

2. **Install dependencies**
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

3. **Environment setup**
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   # Edit .env with your database credentials and JWT secrets
   ```

4. **Database setup**
   ```bash
   # Generate Prisma client
   npx prisma generate

   # Run database migrations
   npx prisma migrate dev

   # (Optional) Seed the database
   npx prisma db seed
   ```

5. **Start the development server**
   ```bash
   npm run start:dev
   ```

The application will be available at `http://localhost:3000`

## 🐳 Docker Setup

### Development with Docker

1. **Start development environment**
   ```bash
   docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
   ```

2. **Run database migrations**
   ```bash
   docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec app-dev npx prisma migrate dev
   ```

### Production with Docker

1. **Build and start production environment**
   ```bash
   docker-compose up -d
   ```

2. **Run database migrations**
   ```bash
   docker-compose exec app npx prisma migrate deploy
   ```

## 📚 API Documentation

Once the application is running, you can access the interactive API documentation at:
- **Swagger UI**: `http://localhost:3000/api`
- **Health Check**: `http://localhost:3000/health`

### Key API Endpoints

#### Authentication
- `POST /auth/register` - Register a new user
- `POST /auth/login` - User login
- `POST /auth/refresh` - Refresh JWT token

#### Products
- `GET /products` - List products with pagination and filtering
- `POST /products` - Create a new product (vendors only)
- `GET /products/:id` - Get product details
- `PUT /products/:id` - Update product (vendor/admin only)
- `DELETE /products/:id` - Delete product (vendor/admin only)

#### Orders
- `POST /orders` - Create a new order
- `GET /orders/customer/:customerId` - Get customer orders
- `GET /orders/vendor/:vendorId` - Get vendor orders
- `PUT /orders/:id/status` - Update order status (admin only)

#### Chat
- `POST /chat/send` - Send a message
- `GET /chat/history/:userId` - Get chat history with a user

## 💬 Real-Time Features

#### Order Notifications
- **Event**: `orderStatusChange`
- **Payload**: Order status update information

- **Event**: `message`
- **Payload**: Chat message data

- **DIRECT**: Direct messaging between users
- **SUPPORT**: Customer/vendor to admin support
- **VENDOR_SUPPORT**: Customer to specific vendor support

# Development Dockerfile with hot reload
FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies for hot reload
RUN npm install -g nodemon

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install all dependencies (including dev dependencies)
RUN npm install

# Copy Prisma schema
COPY prisma ./prisma/

# Generate Prisma client
RUN npx prisma generate

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Create uploads directory
RUN mkdir -p uploads

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application in development mode with hot reload
CMD ["npm", "run", "start:dev"]

# Use Node.js LTS version
FROM node:18-alpine AS base

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./
COPY prisma ./prisma/

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production && npm cache clean --force

# Generate Prisma client
RUN npx prisma generate

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Build the application
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:18-alpine AS production

WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install only production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production && npm cache clean --force

# Copy built application and Prisma schema
COPY --from=base /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=base /app/node_modules/.prisma ./node_modules/.prisma
COPY --from=base /app/prisma ./prisma

# Create non-root user
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs
RUN adduser -S nestjs -u 1001

# Change ownership of app directory
RUN chown -R nestjs:nodejs /app
USER nestjs

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "dist/main"]
